analysis.title: US Equity Strategy 3Q26 Earnings Brief: October 21
key_insights: GE delivered a broad beat with EPS of $2.25 vs $2.01 consensus and revenue of $13.29bn vs $12.86bn consensus, driven by a 23% yoy increase in CES orders.
GE raised FY2026 guidance to EPS of $8.00-$8.10 (vs $7.65-$7.85 previously) and operating profit of $10.9-$11.0bn (vs $10.55-$10.75bn previously).

NFLX reported EPS of $0.87 vs $0.82 consensus, with revenue largely in line at $12.87bn. Q4 revenue guidance of $13.44bn is below the $13.51bn consensus, driven by weaker expected advertising revenue.

SPCX is not in the S&P 500. It reported EPS of $0.37 vs $0.13 consensus and revenue of $14.58bn vs $12.87bn consensus, driven by AI compute leasing revenue of $7.56bn vs $6.3bn consensus. UBS calls this a positive read-through for the AI theme.

Expected 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth is 26.9% yoy. On aggregate, earnings are beating estimates by 4.9% so far, with 78% of companies topping projections. EPS is on pace for 30.1%, assuming the historical trend of estimate revisions through the end of the season.
Expected 3Q EPS growth yoy by group: TECH+ 46.1%, Financials 7.8%, Non-Cyclicals 3.4%, Energy 131.5%. The Cyclicals ex-Energy figure prints as '15.%' in the text.

The six largest TECH+ companies are expected to lag the rest of the market as a group (EPS growth 21.4% vs 28.8%). Individual forecasts: NVDA 89.0%, MSFT 14.3%, GOOG 6.3%, AAPL 5.5%, AMZN 1.8%, META -20.3%.

Consensus implies only Energy and TECH+ outpace the S&P 500 in 3Q, while Health Care is a drag. On a median basis, Energy and Tech+ show the strongest growth, and the median company is expected to outgrow the cap-weighted index in 5 of 11 groups.
3Q26 EPS revisions have improved over the last 3 months, unlike the usual pattern of estimates falling into reporting season. The overhang from ex-Tech may be subsiding.
2026 EPS revisions have stayed strong through 1Q and 2Q, including ex-Tech, which had historically been revised down 5%. Consensus 2026E S&P 500 EPS growth is 28.7%.
Over the next 5 trading days, 109 companies representing 17.0% of S&P 500 market cap report, including Meta Platforms, Tesla, Procter & Gamble, Western Digital, Newmont, Visa and Coca-Cola.
UBS adjusted BAC reported EPS of $0.91 for a $1.2bn anti-money-laundering settlement charge, and JPM reported EPS of $5.57 for $658 million of investment securities losses.

market_movers.rationale: GE beat on EPS ($2.25 vs $2.01) and revenue ($13.29bn vs $12.86bn) and raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $8.00-$8.10. The disclosure table lists a Buy rating and a $299.87 price on 20 Oct 2026.
NFLX beat modestly on EPS ($0.87 vs $0.82) but guided Q4 revenue to $13.44bn vs $13.51bn consensus on weaker advertising.
SPCX beat on EPS ($0.37 vs $0.13) and revenue ($14.58bn vs $12.87bn), with AI compute leasing revenue of $7.56bn vs $6.3bn consensus.

sector_views.rationale: Energy 3Q EPS growth is expected at 131.5% yoy, and consensus has Energy outpacing the S&P 500.
TECH+ 3Q EPS growth is expected at 46.1% yoy, and TECH+ remains a positive for S&P 500 earnings. The six largest TECH+ names are expected to lag the rest of the market.
Consensus expects Health Care to be a drag on 3Q earnings.

earnings_insights: GE 3Q26 reported EPS $2.25 vs consensus $2.01, revenue $13.29bn vs consensus $12.86bn. Orders for CES rose 23% yoy. FY2026 EPS guidance raised to $8.00-$8.10 from $7.65-$7.85, and operating profit guidance to $10.9-$11.0bn from $10.55-$10.75bn.
NFLX 3Q26 reported EPS $0.87 vs consensus $0.82, revenue $12.87bn roughly in line with consensus. Q4 revenue guidance $13.44bn vs consensus $13.51bn on weaker advertising.
SPCX 3Q26 reported EPS $0.37 vs consensus $0.13, revenue $14.58bn vs consensus $12.87bn. AI compute leasing revenue $7.56bn vs consensus $6.3bn.
S&P 500 3Q26 so far: earnings beating estimates by 4.9% on aggregate, 78% of companies beating. Blended EPS growth is 26.9% yoy, on pace for 30.1% with the usual estimate-revision trend.

UBS-adjusted figures: BAC reported EPS $0.91 includes a $1.2bn AML settlement charge, and JPM reported EPS $5.57 includes $658 million of investment securities losses. Both are adjusted higher in UBS tables.
Upcoming within 5 trading days: 109 S&P 500 companies (17.0% of market cap), including META, TSLA, PG, WDC, NEM, V and KO.
risk_factors: The six largest TECH+ companies are expected to lag the market in 3Q EPS growth (21.4% vs 28.8%), with META at -20.3%.
Health Care is expected to be a drag on 3Q earnings.
UBS's risk statement cites macro variables (GDP growth, inflation), economic slowdown, a weakening currency, global events and government policy changes.
